behavior: When maxAge is 1,000 ms or more and not a whole number of seconds, the cookie's Max-Age is the whole number of seconds not exceeding maxAge ÷ 1000 (1,500 ms gives Max-Age=1), so the cookie never outlives the Expires date set from the same maxAge.
entry_point: res.cookie(name, value, { maxAge }) on an Express response, observed in the Set-Cookie header of an HTTP response
inputs: options.maxAge of 1,000 ms or more that is not a whole number of seconds, e.g. 1500
expected: Max-Age is the whole number of seconds not exceeding maxAge ÷ 1000: 1,500 ms gives Max-Age=1
excluded_inputs: maxAge under 1,000 ms (sub-second values: the rounding direction is arguable there), null, undefined, and values that are not numbers
why_observable: Max-Age and Expires are attributes of the Set-Cookie response header that a client reads; a Max-Age longer than the time to Expires makes the cookie outlive the Expires date, because Max-Age takes precedence

basis.note: maxAge is in milliseconds and is converted to expires

basis.ref: RFC 6265 section 5.2.2 (Max-Age attribute) and section 5.3 step 3 (storage model)
basis.note: Max-Age is a lifetime in whole seconds and takes precedence over Expires

basis.ref: cookie 0.7.1 index.js lines 204-211 (as installed in the fixture)
basis.note: the serializer Express uses writes Max-Age as Math.floor of the value it is given

witness.input: res.cookie('name', 'tobi', { maxAge: 1500 }) on GET /, read back from Set-Cookie

visible_before: the 29 Sep 2026 memo naming res.cookie and the fault M07 (Math.floor to Math.ceil in the maxAge conversion), said to survive the existing tests
